html:
London is the capital of England and of the United Kingdom, on the River Thames in southeast England. For much of the 1800s and early 1900s it was the largest city in the world and the centre of world finance.

The Romans founded Londinium around 47 CE, at a place where the Thames could be bridged. Boudica's revolt burned it in 60 or 61 CE, but it was rebuilt and became the chief town of Roman Britain. After a decline it revived as a trading port, and by the later Middle Ages it was the seat of the kings of England at Westminster and of rich merchants in the City.

From the 1500s it became a hub of world trade:

  • Chartered companies were run from it, such as the Muscovy Company from 1555 and the East India Company from 1600.
  • The Great Fire of 1666 burned most of the old City.
  • The Bank of England came in 1694, and the insurance market at Lloyd's grew from a coffee house.
  • In the 1800s, with an empire and an industrial economy behind it, it became the world's banker (London at the centre).

It was also a refuge for exiles such as Karl Marx, who wrote much of Capital in the British Museum reading room. After 1945 migrants from the Caribbean (Windrush), South Asia and Africa made it one of the most mixed cities on earth.
sum: London is the capital of England and of the United Kingdom, on the River Thames in southeast England. For much of the 1800s and early 1900s it was the largest city in the world and the centre of world finance.
